_note: filename -> [top%, bottom%] of the FACE BAND: the top of the highest hat
or hairline to the lowest chin, as a percentage of the published frame's
height. Read by scripts/build_banners.py and published into
docs/data/<group>/banners.json as 'face_band'.
WHY IT IS PUBLISHED AND NOT JUST WRITTEN DOWN. Every focal in focal.json
is derived from this measurement, and the masthead's height cap is bounded
from below by it -- a band shorter than (bottom - top) x the frame's
rendered height cannot hold the faces at any object-position. Until now
that number lived in commit messages and in one person's head, so nothing
could check it. With it in the manifest, test_banners.py computes the
floor for the whole set and fails the build if a new banner or a re-crop
ever pushes it above the cap in style.css.
HOW TO MEASURE ONE. Overlay the published image with a 5% horizontal grid
and read two numbers off it: the highest point of any manager's hair or
hat, and the lowest point of any manager's chin. Hands, shoulders and
equipment do not count -- this band is about faces, because a cut face is
the failure being prevented and a cut elbow is not.
Optional by contract, like alt and focal. Absent means the cap floor
cannot be checked for that image, which is why the test also asserts that
every published banner carries one.
